prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering. Operations Control Centre: Line Traffic Controller regulates service/approved timetables; dispatch station-holds affect departure,not route-locking. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern),non-vital: sends Crew Login Token Bundle; confirms options; uses controller-consistent station/platform identifiers; reconciles deviations/closures/crowding before passenger release. Service Timetable Server supplies approved schedules/platform-use context. Passenger Information Gateway receives operational state/timetable-reconciled predictions/stopping-pattern/platform-allocation updates; destination/skip-stop publication requires CBTC-confirmed identity/route. Closed-platform movements remain tracked,but unavailable-for-boarding. Local station staff indications require validated CBTC states: normal/held/door-interlock-fault/radio-degraded/emergency-stop/evacuation-support. Voice Dispatch Console displays calling-identity/platform/hold-reason; Revenue Train Operator must readback instructions,maintain readiness/report hazards; voice cannot replace safety validation. Dispatch requires positive confirmation/cancellation,distinct from timeout/failure/rejection. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid) cover northern/southern mainlines/turnbacks. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking retain locking/release authority; send vital point/occupancy/locking states. Zones require proved/locked points,overlap/flank/conflict protection,boundary vacancy; mismatch/axle-counter conflict restricts authority within braking-envelope. Falcon sends Axle Counter Reset Request; routes/approaches inhibit reset; Maple(unidentified) verifies/records clearance. West sends Route Release Exception List; hazards persist until excluded. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout; validates messages/enforces authority/speed/doors/braking; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; reports door-enable-side/berth/departure-readiness. Dual Channel Odometer divergence degrades separation; transfers require position/receiving-zone validation,isolation/brake-feedback assurance. Train Radio Modem reports connectivity; requires Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before renewed station/passenger secure sessions. Wayside Radio Access Network(Saffron) sends Radio Handover Audit File; maintains station-message paths through transitions/recovery; degradation retains validated authority. Safety Data Communication Network segregates safety-station/nonvital-passenger traffic; authenticated/integrity-protected/deterministic; sends Clock Drift Sample Report to Cryptographic Key

New part:
S150: During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
S151: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
S152: Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
S153: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
S154: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
S155: Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
S156: The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
S157: The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
S158: Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
S159: The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
S160: The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
S161: The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
S162: The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
S163: The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
S164: The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
S165: The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
S166: A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
